0 · Ground truth — the shipped icon

mobile/assets/icon.png — app icon, splash and notification icon, used as the identity reference (our own IP). Two things about it are load-bearing and were each got wrong at least once:

  • Eyes are solid neon pink — no pupil, no iris, no white.
  • He glares on purpose. An early round prompted the smug brow out for a “friendly guide”, producing an off-model character. It was put back.

2 · point — three versions

Two separate problems, fixed in sequence. First direction: “points right” failed five times across two models, and only a geometric description — “the snout is nearest the right edge” — worked. Then shape: that fix produced a real three-quarter turn, which grew a muzzle. The resolution was to stop rotating the head at all and carry direction by sliding features across the flat face.

v1 · nano_banana_pro

True three-quarter turn. Direction read fine, but it grew a protruding muzzle and jaw the other five poses do not have — it stopped being a football.

v2 · nano_banana

Muzzle gone, football silhouette restored by shifting laces and eyes across the flat face instead of rotating. But composition drifted right and clipped the far horn.

v3 · nano_banana — SHIPPED

Same approach, framing pinned: centred, nothing cropped, direction still unmistakable and correct when mirrored.

3 · thinking — four versions

The most-iterated pose. “Looking up and away” is conventionally drawn with pupils, so the model kept reintroducing an eyeball however the negative prompt was phrased. Changing model and separating the two problems — eyes first, then rotation — solved it.

v1 · nano_banana_pro

Both eyes show a lighter oval reading as a pupil; head barely tilted.

v2 · nano_banana_pro — fix round

One eye cleaned, the other kept a faint pupil; tilt still weak.

v3 · nano_banana

Eyes finally clean both sides — but the head over-rotated ~45°, reading as falling over.

v4 · nano_banana — SHIPPED

Tilt dialled to ~10°, upright and centred, sceptical brows, doubtful mouth.

4 · The flat set — built, then retired

A full flat set was generated so the medium could be chosen on real evidence rather than a stale off-model sheet. D-156 chose painted, so this is reference art now — kept because it is the ready-made answer if 44 pt legibility ever becomes a real complaint.

flat neutral · nano_banana_pro

The flat exploration at its best — genuinely flat, same character and attitude. nano_banana could not do flat at all; it kept the gradients and added white banding.

flat point · failed

Two attempts at a flat point: the first would not turn at all, this one lost an eye. Unresolved when the flat arm was retired.

Flat @ 44 pt — holds its read.

Painted @ 44 pt — collapses. The accepted cost of D-156.

5 · The three style arms

Generated before the per-pose work to choose a medium. All predate the no-pupil and menacing-expression fixes, so the faces are off-model — read them for rendering style only.

A — logo-match painted. The arm that shipped.

Blend — icon identity, flat rendering. Became the flat set above.

C — Chalkline-minimal. Heavily simplified; loses the most likeness.

6 · Discarded rounds

The “friendly neutral” error — glare prompted out — plus pupils in several eyes.

The strawman: the flat arm run once on seedream_v4_5, which ignored the flat-shading constraint — gradients, an invented white muzzle, a phone frame with a status bar, a visor prop. A model failure, not evidence about the flat style, and why every later arm ran on one model.
